questions.question_text: In 'What a Bird Thought', what is the primary takeaway highlighted in the text?

questions.marking_scheme_answer: Definition: Settled snugly, comfortably, and warmly.. Example: And nestled by my mother.

questions.question_text: Provide a detailed summary (80-100 words) of 'What a Bird Thought', highlighting the character actions and moral outcome.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The bird's journey begins inside a small pale-blue eggshell, representing the sheltered boundaries of infancy. Moving to a straw nest, its world expands to immediate family care. Perched on a leafy branch, it realizes its earlier blindness as it discovers nature. Finally, soaring into the sky, it acknowledges that the world is an infinite mystery. This parallels human intellectual growth from early childhood home life to broad global awareness.

questions.question_text: Short Question: Why does the bird ask 'can you?' at the end of the poem?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Model Answer: To invite the reader to reflect on the endless vastness and mystery of the universe.. Marking points: Invites reader reflection, Emphasizes vastness of nature, Highlights mystery of creation.

questions.question_text: Guided Writing Extension: Write a paragraph on 'How my view of the world expanded as I grew up'.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Format: Perspective Paragraph. Key Value Points: Early childhood view, School experiences, Realization of wider world.
Sample Output: When I was five, my world was just my home and playground. But as I started school, read books, and studied science, my mind flew beyond my neighborhood. I realized the world is filled with diverse cultures, oceans, and stars!

questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Plot Summary: The bird recalls its infancy inside a small, pale-blue eggshell, believing the entire world was small and round.
